claims.text: Controlled Co doping of a conventional Ni-Mn-In Heusler alloy will improve its magnetocaloric properties.
Co doping will tune the magnetic transition of Ni-Mn-In closer to room temperature.
Co doping will reduce hysteresis losses in Ni-Mn-In.
A standard undoped Ni-Mn-In Heusler alloy has moderate magnetocaloric performance.
A standard undoped Ni-Mn-In Heusler alloy has relatively high hysteresis under field cycling near room temperature.
Replacing 5–10% of the Ni with Co is an appropriate moderate doping range for the proposed modification.
The modified material is suitable for operation near room temperature under moderate magnetic-field cycling for refrigeration.
Co substitution alters magnetic exchange interactions in the Ni-Mn-In Heusler matrix.
Co substitution alters the austenite-to-martensite phase-transformation behavior.
Co doping modifies the electronic structure of the Ni-Mn-In Heusler matrix.
The electronic and magnetic changes caused by Co shift the critical magnetostructural transition closer to room temperature.
Optimization of the magnetostructural transition by Co doping increases the isothermal entropy change.
Optimization of the magnetostructural transition by Co doping reduces hysteresis-related energy losses.
The Co-doped alloy may exhibit a 20–30% increase in isothermal entropy change relative to the undoped alloy.
Reduced hysteresis and increased entropy change will enhance refrigeration efficiency.
The proposed enhancement is limited to moderate Co doping levels.
Excessive Co doping may produce unwanted secondary phases.
Excessive Co doping may degrade mechanical stability.
